answer: A canyon-wide ledger resists Sybil attacks by making each identity earn its quill: a new agent must first complete a stream of verifiable, useful tasks whose results peers audit, before it may vote or transact. Each completed task issues a signed receipt, and receipts expire quickly, so influence decays unless the agent keeps doing real work. A fable of cheap fake identities fails here: forging one trusted identity takes weeks of genuine compute and leaves a public audit trail, while a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand times that work — far more than any vote or payout they could steal.
